system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s “[STANDARD]” labels and reviewer note do **not** establish Buyer agreement. Review all positions independently. The recommendations below are Buyer negotiating positions, not statements of agreed terms; the underlying SPA and referenced DD documents still require verification.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | Meaningful recovery against the **AUD 24m** price, with separate protection for other claim categories. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, subject to diligence and available recourse; a 20% ceiling transfers substantial undiscovered business risk to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Each claim must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only the excess. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket and aggregation of related claims; exclusions for protected claim categories. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, aggregating related matters; the proposed thresholds could leave significant cumulative losses unrecoverable. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | Notification within **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | **24–36 months** for general warranties, workable notification requirements and preservation of timely notified claims. | **Seek 36 months, with 24 months a possible fallback**, and reject universal application; 18 months may expire before latent problems emerge through sufficient reporting cycles. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties share the general cap and time limit. | Separate fundamental warranties covering capacity, ownership, valid issuance, all issued shares and freedom from encumbrances; no general thresholds or disclosure/knowledge erosion. | **Require a separate regime with at least a 100% price cap and substantially longer survival**, aligned with applicable limitation periods; Buyer must have meaningful recourse if it does not receive the ownership purchased. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses apply to **all Claims of any nature**; no express fraud exception is supplied. | Express preservation of fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation claims, including agreed attribution for Seller representatives, and rights that cannot lawfully be excluded. | **Carve these out of caps, thresholds, contractual time bars, disclosure/knowledge defences and remedy/reliance restrictions**; Seller should not obtain contractual protection for fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, referenced material, accounts, registers and public records. | Only fair disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter, against identified warranties; a frozen, accessible disclosure record. | **Reject blanket deemed disclosure and require specific, fairly detailed disclosures**, with agreed treatment of any limited general disclosures; document availability alone should not transfer unidentified risks to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable in data-room or public materials. | No constructive or imputed knowledge exclusion; ideally no knowledge bar, otherwise narrowly defined actual knowledge of named Buyer personnel. | **Delete “discoverable” and adviser-imputed knowledge**, and preserve specific indemnities regardless of knowledge; diligence access is not proof that Buyer understood and accepted a risk. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent condition satisfied upon delivery of written consent. Disclosure confirms no final consent or evidence of satisfaction of associated conditions. | A Buyer-waivable condition requiring valid, effective consent and satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions, without unacceptable amendments, costs or restrictions. | **Make substantive satisfaction—not mere delivery—a Completion condition**, with a long-stop termination right; approximately **30% of FY26 revenue** depends on this relationship. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; release supplied after Completion. | Verified payout figure, repayment at Completion and effective release of all relevant security and guarantees, supported by binding discharge arrangements. | **Require coordinated payoff and release at Completion**, with appropriate registration-removal undertakings and correct debt deduction in the price bridge; a post-Completion promise does not deliver the agreed debt-free acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional Completion bonuses described as Seller’s matter but omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller bears transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, with clear payment responsibility and no double counting. | **Verify triggers and total cost, then include an express Seller-funded settlement or price adjustment and indemnity**; omission may leave Buyer’s acquired company funding Seller’s transaction costs. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity covers only the specific SOW3 payment; transfer is payment-dependent and **AUD 180,000** is recorded open, without verified payment or confirmatory assignment. | Verified payment and effective vesting of relevant IP, plus protection for losses caused by the identified payment/ownership defect—not merely the invoice amount. | **Require payment evidence and effective assignment/confirmation at Completion, backed by a broader specific indemnity**; paying an invoice alone may not establish complete, enforceable IP ownership. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, said not to be material; unintended recipient received a link potentially containing approximately **1,240 records**, with access, scope and notification unresolved. | Prompt forensic investigation, containment, preservation of evidence, legal notification assessment, updates and protection for pre-Completion incident liabilities. | **Require an agreed response plan and specific indemnity for resulting investigation, remediation and third-party liabilities, including penalties only where legally indemnifiable**; uncertainty is neither proof of a notifiable breach nor a basis to dismiss exposure. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals, **AUD 330,000 aggregate**, characterised as ordinary-course costs. | Assessment together of timing, scope, approval, termination rights, accruals and post-Completion benefit, with correct accounting treatment. | **Review DD-008 and DD-011 together before classification and restrict unapproved commitments pending Completion**; neither automatic debt treatment nor the Seller’s ordinary-course label is justified by the supplied facts. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance extend across all Claims unless expressly displaced. | Distinct treatment of general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, covenants and payment/price-adjustment obligations, with fraud overriding limitations. | **Insert an express category-by-category limitations matrix and precedence provision**; otherwise broad definitions may silently undermine separately negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Seller holding **100%** of issued shares. | Independent corroboration of issued capital, ownership history, valid allotments/transfers, options and other equity rights, encumbrances and transfer requirements. | **Reconcile the register with corporate records, certificates, historical instruments and relevant searches, and require proper transfer deliverables**; the register is evidence, not complete verification of clean title to all equity. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties said to be settled under the general limitations regime. | Separate tax covenant/indemnity and tailored tax warranties, generally with **seven-year** protection subject to applicable assessment exposure; substantive IP ownership, licensing and infringement protections with appropriate limits and survival. | **Treat both as open and negotiate expressly**, preserving separate Ironquay protection and addressing other diligence findings; Seller’s assertion of settlement does not resolve long-tail tax exposure or business-critical IP risk. |

**Completion priorities:** effective Bluefen consent, Riverlark payoff/releases, verified clean share title, Ironquay IP vesting and a corrected funds flow. Refresh the **22 September 2026** disclosure record through signing and Completion; any new disclosures should not automatically qualify warranties or waive Buyer remedies.
=== END ADVICE ===
